sections.overview: The Netted Mountain Moth is listed here as Macaria carbonaria, but a 2024 molecular revision transferred it to Epelis carbonaria.
sections.identification: It is a small geometrid moth; the British account gives a wingspan of about 23–25 mm.
sections.habitat: In Britain it is known from Scottish Highland moorland and mountain slopes, while European records also include heathland and raised bogs.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed on bearberry; a Norwegian account also lists bog-rosemary as a host plant.
sections.behavior: Adults fly by day in spring and early summer and visit flowers growing in the habitat.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted identify its larval host plants but do not give a verified clutch size or brood count.
sections.ecology: Unlike the bilberry-feeding Rannoch Looper, now placed in Speranza, this species is associated with bearberry and other northern heath or bog plants.
sections.conservation: A Scottish site review describes it as confined in Britain to the Highlands and notes low dispersal and vulnerability to habitat change; these are regional, historically based observations.
